answer_text:
Let

\[
f(x)=x^3+3x^2+5x+7.
\]

Its roots are \(a,b,c\). By Vieta’s formulas,

\[
a+b+c=-3.
\]

Thus

\[
b+c=(a+b+c)-a=-3-a,
\]

and similarly,

\[
a+c=-3-b,\qquad a+b=-3-c.
\]

The given conditions therefore become

\[
P(a)=-3-a,\quad P(b)=-3-b,\quad P(c)=-3-c.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
P(a)+a+3=0,\quad P(b)+b+3=0,\quad P(c)+c+3=0.
\]

Define

\[
Q(x)=P(x)+x+3.
\]

Then

\[
Q(a)=Q(b)=Q(c)=0.
\]

Since \(P(x)\) is cubic, \(Q(x)\) is also cubic. The cubic polynomial \(f(x)\) has the same roots \(a,b,c\), and \(f(x)\) is monic, so

\[
Q(x)=k f(x)
\]

for some constant \(k\). Therefore,

\[
P(x)=k f(x)-x-3.
\]

Now use the condition \(P(a+b+c)=-16\). Since \(a+b+c=-3\),

\[
P(-3)=-16.
\]

Compute

\[
f(-3)=(-3)^3+3(-3)^2+5(-3)+7
=-27+27-15+7=-8.
\]

Thus

\[
P(-3)=k(-8)-(-3)-3=-8k.
\]

So

\[
-8k=-16 \implies k=2.
\]

Hence

\[
P(x)=2f(x)-x-3.
\]

Finally,

\[
P(0)=2f(0)-0-3=2(7)-3=14-3=11.
\]

\[
\boxed{11}
\]
